hook: AI gave you a 400-word essay when you needed a one-line answer. Again.
caption:
AI gave you a 400-word essay when you needed a one-line answer. Again.

Here's what's actually happening:

ChatGPT doesn't know if you're a "give me the bottom line" person or a "walk me through every step" person. So it guesses. And it usually guesses wrong — defaulting to the safest, most thorough, most exhausting response possible.

It's not broken. It just doesn't know you.

The fix isn't reprompting every single time. The fix is teaching it once.

There's a specific phrase that changes everything:

"I'm a bottom-line-first thinker. Lead with the answer, then give me 1-2 sentences of context max. Only expand if I ask."

Paste that at the start of a new chat and watch the whole vibe shift.

This is literally what bootfile.ai automates — it figures out your thinking style (are you a Synthesizer? A Validator? A Sprinter?) and builds a profile that tells AI how your brain actually works.

So you stop re-explaining yourself every time you open a new tab.

Small change. Wildly different results.
